mathematical_assessment: The atomic statement is uniform in all internal j,a,b, including nonstandard values. Only fixed templates are externally finite; compilation and the prior slot/numOK results handle internal indices.

The final proof supplies all eight premises of atomG: two slot statements, two numeral-correctness statements, matching functionality, two uniqueness statements and the atom-definition statement. No hSchema or general glue theorem is assumed.
GF is forall t (not M_j(t) or (atom iff environment_atom(t))). The theorem retains this matching antecedent and does not assert that a matching environment exists.

The semantic proofs of the two fixed logical templates use all template models and completeness, then compiledG transports their finite proofs to internal formulas; they are not a standard-natural-number model check.

Membership/equality and specialization indices are consistent with EnvTransform.memXYS/eqXYS, which read vector positions1/0. The extra ignored environment argument is retained through the two specializations.

No sorry/admit/axiom declaration or enlarged proof-limit option was introduced. No obvious mathematical/API reference defect was found by source review; elaboration and axiom census were not checked here.
frontier_effect: Closes the explicit positive atomic compiled-glue client under the existing matching predicate. Numeral correctness and slot functionality are now consumed in this client, rather than left as atomic premises.
remaining_obligations: Connect this atom-specific typed statement and eAtomT_val to the general syntactic relativize/envForm invariant, including the atomic constructor code identities and free-variable bound.
